correctness.rationale: For finite connected undirected positive weighted graphs, b>0 and 0<epsilon<b/(b+dmax), the clipped-sign flow is negative gradient of E(x)=x^TLx/2+b||x||²/2-b sum F_epsilon(x_i). At central or kink coordinate the inward central second derivative d_i+b-b/epsilon<0, contradicting local minimum at an attracting equilibrium, so all attracting states occupy strict plateaus. There x=H_b s with H_b=b(L+bI)^-1 strictly positive row stochastic. Stationarity and -L-bI local Jacobian imply exact if-and-only-if count by s_i(H_b s)_i>epsilon. A single dissenter i is stable iff H_ii>(1+epsilon)/2, and all 2^n patterns attract iff the least H_ii crosses this strict cutoff. On K1,5 with b=2,epsilon=1/10, H_hub=3/8<11/20 and H_leaf=17/24>11/20, yielding leaf-only but not hub-only stable dissent. This classifies asymptotically stable equilibria, not basins, other states or out-of-regime dynamics.
residual_risks: Strict central slope is essential and not interchangeable with eps<1; no global basin theorem.
Original model primary paper full text could not be obtained (institutional VPN disconnected).
